subject: Copywriting
title: Town Criers: The Human Billboard
description: A micro-lesson that makes Town Criers: The Human Billboard usable.

hook.text: Before newspapers, towns hired people to shout the news. Town criers were the first broadcast medium.

buildup.text: Criers announced royal decrees, market prices, and merchant offers. Their voice was the only ad channel.

discovery.text: The best criers used rhythm and rhyme. Catchy phrases stuck in minds—early jingles, spoken aloud.

twist.text: Criers were licensed by the king. Unauthorized shouting was illegal. Ad regulation started early.

climax.text: When the printing press arrived, criers faded. But their lesson survived: memorable beats forgettable.

punchline.text: The first ad men didn't write. They shouted.

quiz.question: What made town criers effective advertisers?
